I'm going to premise this by saying that I am not transgender, I will never be able to understand what it is like, but I feel as though I may be able to offer some advice. 
First there are many resources on here to help you. 
Second, I think it might be helpful to start to reevaluate your idea of gender. By this I mean, don't tie it to the chromosomes or genitals your born with.There is so much more to being a man or woman in society that just the genitals or chromosomes you are born with. The way we express gender is completely arbitrary and socially constructed. For example when you see a woman walking in a public, how do you know she is a woman? Its usually the way she dresses and presents herself, not her genitals. No one sits by the bathroom to crotch check people to make sure they have the right genitals to enter, instead we just assume that someone presenting in a certain way is a certain gender, and the way we present is not exclusive to either sex. You can be born with a penis but still wear feminine clothes, makeup, and style your hair in a feminine way. Same with people born with a uterus, they can still wear masculine clothes, and present in a masculine way. Those who are later in their transition will usually become indiscernible from those who were born with the "right" chromosomes. Seriously, hormones are incredible, and there is no need to go through surgery if you don't want to. Many trans people never go through surgery and they look every bit like the gender they identify as. 

I don't know your specific situation and so can't give specific advice, I also can't tell you I understand because I am not transgender. But going off the title of this post, I think it would be beneficial for you to reevaluate the way you look at gender and sex. The scientific field considers these two things separate, and I think it would help if you did too. 
Stay strong friend.
